searchText: what is the exact problem with adding instructions with immediates? obviously adding new instructions potentially changes the behavior of deployed contracts that had assumed those were invalid opcodes, yet we do that all the time. how is adding instructions _with immediates_ different? ok i think the issue is it may change decoding/parsing entirely and may introduce new jumpdests. eg: `XX 60 5B`is `invalid push1 0x5b`, and if we make `XX` an instruction with 1 byte immediate then this becomes `xx 0x60 jumpdest`, and there's probably arbitrarily worse changes that can happen as in modifying even more subsequent instructions is this it? is there anything else? have we explored fixing this by making the range 60-7F invalid bytes in immediates? 5B also needs to be rejected to avoid masking a preexisting jumpdest
